narrative.h2: YouTube is the one platform where the full-length MV still wins

sections.heading: Why 16:9 and longer-form still matter here
sections.body: Outside YouTube, the music video has been compressed into vertical 60-second clips. On YouTube, the original format is still the dominant one — 16:9, 3-to-5 minutes, watched on a TV or laptop in the background. The platform's algorithm rewards watch time in minutes, not retention in seconds, which means a 4-minute MV that holds 60% is worth more than ten 30-second cuts that hold 90%. The math favors letting the song breathe.

sections.heading: What the YouTube MV canon looks like
sections.body: Open with a cold intro (Hiro Murai's Childish Gambino videos, Dave Meyers' 21 Savage cuts, anything Cole Bennett directs for Lyrical Lemonade) — 5 to 15 seconds of scene-setting before the first downbeat. Hold establishing wides longer than you would on TikTok. Earn the close-up. End with a tag, an outro card, or a smash cut to credits — the YouTube viewer is conditioned to watch through the end card.

sections.heading: Tunee's YouTube preset, specifically
sections.body: Pick YouTube and the renderer outputs 16:9 at 4K, with a longer intro window, slower average cut length (1.8 seconds versus 0.9 for the TikTok preset), and a chaptered timeline if your song has clear sections. Upload-ready MP4, H.264, audio at 320 kbps AAC. Thumbnail-frame grabs at the visual peaks are auto-generated so you're not scrubbing the timeline trying to find the moment that sells the click.
